correctness.summary: A two-regime proof establishes the fixed-gradient factor 1/[(u^TBu)(u^TB^{-1}u)] for every trust radius. The boundary regime reduces the desired domination to an affine function of normalized radius whose endpoints follow from Cauchy-Schwarz and AM-GM. Kantorovich gives the sharp condition-number envelope, and explicit two-dimensional equality families plus deterministic numerical checks verify sharpness and limiting cases.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Checked trust-region sources treat the Cauchy point, fraction-of-Cauchy decrease, exact trust-region minimization, and fraction-of-optimal decrease, while Kantorovich gives the classical unconstrained steepest-descent factor. Searches under exact, synonymous, and condition-number formulations did not locate the radius-uniform sharp ratio or the resulting sharp SPD conversion from fraction-of-Cauchy to fraction-of-optimal decrease. Broad classical monographs and older Powell-era literature remain a material residual historical-equivalence risk.

value.summary: The theorem provides a sharp radius-independent certificate against the exact SPD trust-region optimum and turns the standard fraction-of-Cauchy condition into a sharp fraction-of-optimal condition whenever the quadratic model is uniformly SPD. It also extends directly to fixed SPD trust-region metrics by a change of variables.

limitations: Exact arithmetic and real SPD quadratic models only.
The guarantee concerns predicted quadratic model reduction, not actual reduction of a nonlinear objective or closeness of the steps.
Indefinite models admit no analogous positive universal factor; a negative-curvature counterexample is given.
Exact trust-region, dogleg, Steihaug-CG, Lanczos and related solvers may outperform the Cauchy point; no runtime superiority is claimed.
Broad classical trust-region monographs and older literature leave residual originality risk under different terminology.
Independent audit has not been performed.
